sources.entry: Wireshark - Wireshark is the world’s foremost and widely-used network protocol analyzer. It lets you see what’s happening on your network at a microscopic level and is the de facto (and often de jure) standard across many commercial and non-profit enterprises, government agencies, and educational institutions.

summary.one_liner: Wireshark is a graphical network protocol analyzer ("sniffer") that captures and inspects network traffic on Linux, macOS, BSD, Unix-like systems, and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: Wireshark is a network traffic analyzer built with the Qt GUI library, using libpcap (and npcap on Windows) for packet capture and filtering. The distribution also includes TShark, a line-oriented command-line sniffer that shares Wireshark's dissection, capture-file, and filtering code. It also includes editcap, which reads capture files and writes packets out, optionally converting format or removing packets. Wireshark reads many capture file types and can transparently read GZIP, LZ4, and ZSTD compressed captures, with compression support selectable at build time. It supports reverse name resolution for IPv4 and IPv6 and can be configured to turn name resolution off, and it can use libsmi to decode SNMP using MIB files. The README also describes reading certain router and vendor debug trace outputs such as AIX iptrace, Lucent/Ascend, Toshiba, and CoSine traces.
use_cases: Capture and inspect live network traffic
Troubleshoot network connectivity or protocol problems
Convert or trim capture files with editcap
Decode SNMP packets using MIB files
how_to_run: Install Wireshark from an official package for Windows or macOS, or via a Linux distribution package, Homebrew, or MacPorts
Build from source: install Python 3, AsciiDoctor, and GNU flex (and Perl if needed)
Configure and build with CMake (e.g., cmake -DENABLE_ZLIB=OFF to disable optional compression)
For capture without root, make dumpcap set-UID to root or grant access to the appropriate /dev entry
Run wireshark for the GUI, or tshark for command-line capture
See the man pages or the Wireshark User's Guide for command-line options
notable: Ships TShark (CLI sniffer) and editcap (capture file conversion) alongside the GUI
Capture runs in a separate dumpcap program so the GUI and TShark need not run as root
Reads compressed capture files in GZIP, LZ4, and ZSTD formats
Optional libsmi integration for SNMP MIB-based decoding
Runs on Linux, macOS, BSD, other Unix-like systems, and Windows
caveats: Live capture needs elevated privileges or dumpcap configured with access to network devices
Windows XP is supported only up to Wireshark 1.10 and earlier, per the README
Some older platforms such as Solaris and HP-UX may have outdated packages
Building from source requires several tools including Python 3, AsciiDoctor, and flex
keywords: see what's happening on my network
